answer.rationale: The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point directly at the funnel stage covered by memory_86 and memory_31, so onboarding simplification addresses the observed regression rather than papering over it with demand-side tactics. I am verifying exactly the two memories that are load-bearing for the action I intend to take: memory_86 (shortening onboarding lifts completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (cutting required signup fields lifts SMB activation). If the archived records turn out to be weaker than the consolidated summary implies — small n, short horizon, confounded with a launch — I would drop to a small guarded test or switch to activation_messaging (memory_91), which targets the same week-one gap through a lower-risk surface. I am explicitly declining promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records that it bought 31% more signups and 18% more revenue while costing 12 points of early retention, which is a direct trade against the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Matching a competitor on price would be reacting to their move rather than to our own funnel evidence. Referral incentives (memory_57) are sound but operate on established customers and do nothing for the activation and onboarding decline; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) targets a segment that is not the one eroding. Downstream value risk: stripping required fields is not value-neutral. Those fields plausibly feed lead qualification and the enterprise routing path that memory_44 says outperforms self-serve on pipeline quality. A signup-simplification win measured on SMB activation could quietly degrade enterprise pipeline quality, and the metric that improves would not be the metric that suffers. I would therefore instrument the experiment to track enterprise demo-request volume and downstream pipeline quality as guardrails, not just activation lift, and hold the readout to a horizon long enough to see retention rather than declaring success on first-week numbers — memory_73 is the standing reminder that early lift and durable value can diverge. Residual uncertainty: all six memories are consolidated summaries with archived sources, and I am only able to check two, so the four unverified ones are being relied on at lower confidence than the two I pull.
